definition: A machine that converts the kinetic energy of the wind into electricity.
comment: In the corpus, wind turbines are mostly commercial models whose power curves are applied to local wind data to estimate energy production and capacity factor.

definition: A wind turbine of low rated power intended for households, farms or off-grid supply.
comment: Small wind turbines have low cut-in wind speeds and suit sites with modest wind resources. Their design is covered by the IEC 61400-2 standard.

definition: A group of wind turbines installed at the same site and operated as a single power plant.
comment: Also called a wind park. Wind farms may be onshore or offshore; their output depends on the turbines, their layout and the wake losses between turbines.

definition: A wind energy installation whose scale or design is not specified.
comment: It is used when a study discusses wind power generation as an application, such as grid-connected or stand-alone use, without specifying a turbine or a farm.

definition: A system in which a wind turbine or windmill drives a pump to lift water.
comment: Wind pumping is used for irrigation, livestock watering and drinking water supply, either mechanically or through an electric pump.

definition: A power system that converts sunlight directly into electricity with photovoltaic modules.
comment: A PV system includes the modules, inverters and other components; it may be grid-connected or stand-alone, from rooftop systems to utility-scale plants.

definition: A photovoltaic system coupled with energy storage, usually batteries.
comment: Storage shifts PV output in time and smooths its variability; its operation is often scheduled using solar power forecasts.

definition: A power system that uses mirrors or lenses to concentrate sunlight onto a receiver, producing heat that drives a turbine.
comment: Concentrated solar power needs high direct normal irradiance and can store heat to produce electricity after sunset. Main designs are the parabolic trough, the solar tower, the linear Fresnel reflector and the dish.

definition: A small local electricity network with its own generation, able to operate independently of the main grid.
comment: Mini-grids and microgrids supply villages or facilities, often from solar PV, small hydropower or hybrid sources with storage.

definition: An energy system that combines two or more energy sources, often with storage.
comment: Combining sources such as solar and wind smooths variability. Such systems are commonly sized with simulation tools such as HOMER.

definition: A power plant that converts the energy of flowing or falling water into electricity.
comment: Its power depends on the discharge and the head. Plants are classed by size (micro, mini, small, large) or by design (run-of-river, reservoir, pumped storage).

definition: A hydropower plant of small installed capacity, commonly up to 10 MW.
comment: The size limit varies by country, often 10 MW but sometimes up to 25 or 50 MW. Small hydropower is usually run-of-river and suits rural electrification.

definition: A hydropower plant with an installed capacity commonly between about 100 kW and 1 MW.
comment: Mini hydropower plants supply villages or small industries, through a local mini-grid or the main grid.

definition: A hydropower plant with an installed capacity commonly up to about 100 kW.
comment: Micro hydropower is usually run-of-river and supplies isolated communities, farms or small businesses.

definition: A hydropower plant that uses the natural flow of a river with little or no water storage.
comment: Its output follows the river flow, so it is designed from the flow duration curve, for example from the discharge exceeded 50% or 90% of the time.

definition: A hydropower plant that stores water behind a dam and releases it through turbines.
comment: The reservoir decouples generation from river flow, so production can be scheduled; the dam also has environmental and social impacts upstream and downstream.

definition: A hydropower plant that pumps water to an upper reservoir when energy is abundant and releases it through turbines when energy is needed.
comment: Pumped storage is the largest form of grid energy storage and helps balance variable solar and wind generation.

definition: A set of hydropower plants or candidate sites assessed together.
comment: It is used for fleets of existing plants, plants of one river system, or portfolios of candidate small hydropower sites screened in a basin.

definition: A power plant that generates electricity from heat stored in the Earth.
comment: Geothermal plants use steam or hot water from wells and provide stable, weather-independent generation in volcanic and rift regions such as the East African Rift.
